title: Pairs Trading with Nonlinear and Non-Gaussian State Space Models

extraction.methodology_summary: This paper models the price spread between two assets as an unobservable, mean-reverting state variable using a nonlinear and non-Gaussian state space framework that incorporates ARCH-style heteroskedasticity and a flexible drift function. The unobserved spread and parameters are estimated via a Quasi Monte Carlo Kalman filter algorithm. A simulation-based approach determines optimal trading boundaries (thresholds) for executing a novel trading strategy (Strategy C) that opens and closes positions based on volatility levels and threshold crossings.
extraction.universe: US banks listed on the NYSE and specific equity pairs / ETFs (PEP vs KO, EWT vs EWH)

performance_metrics.context: PEP vs KO using Strategy C, Model II
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: The results show that the new approach can achieve 21.86% annualized return for the PEP/KO pair

performance_metrics.context: EWT vs EWH using Strategy C, Model II
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: and 31.84% annualized return for the EWT/EWH pair.

performance_metrics.context: PEP/KO pair, Strategy C, Model II
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: we find that our approach achieves an annualized return of 0.2186 and Sharpe ratio of 2.9518 on the PEP/KO pair

performance_metrics.context: EWT/EWH pair, Strategy C, Model II
performance_metrics.evidence_quote: and an annualized return of 0.3184 and Sharpe ratio of 3.8892 on the EWT/EWH pair.
In comparison, a conventional approach applied to the same pairs can only achieve an annualized return of 0.1311 and Sharpe ratio of 1.1003 for the PEP/KO pair
and an annualized return of 0.1480 and Sharpe ratio of 1.1277 for the EWT/EWH pair.

key_findings: Nonlinear and non-Gaussian state space models capture stylized features of asset prices such as heavy-tailedness, heteroskedasticity, and volatility clustering.
The newly proposed trading strategy (Strategy C) combined with Model II significantly outperforms conventional benchmark models and strategies in both return and Sharpe ratio.
Pairs formed among small banks yield higher returns than pairs among large banks due to higher volatility of the spread.
Out-of-sample tests confirm the robustness and superior performance of the proposed nonlinear/non-Gaussian modeling and Strategy C approach.
